A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Selector model is better at generating coherent and fluent summaries, whereas the Classifier model is better at capturing the redundancy of sentences.
the classifier based architecture is better at summarizing longer documents, whereas the selector based architecture is better when documents are short and have more redundancy.
we propose novel architectures that are both interpretable and perform well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of architecture is as important as the choice of model.
it is important to design models that can capture the inherent structure in the problem of summarization, rather than simply learning to predict summary labels.
a neural network architecture that is free to choose the ordering of its summary can outperform a sequential classifier that is forced to make a decision on each sentence in a particular order.
